guide.intro: Pick how you want to use Unslop — both paths end at your first scan result. The progress below is derived live from your account.

github.installApp: The GitHub App posts reviews as native checks on your pull requests. Install it once for your account or organization and choose which repositories it may see.
github.activateRepo: Activating a repository registers it with the Gatekeeper and starts a one-time index of its API surface. Only activated repositories are reviewed.
github.openPr: From now on every pull request is reviewed automatically — findings land as a check run and as review comments on the PR.

cli.installCli: The CLI runs the same review pipeline against your local changes, before anything reaches a pull request.

cli.firstScan: Scans your tracked changes against the merge-base and prints the findings in the terminal — zero configuration.

guide.extensionBody: The extension shows findings directly in the editor and lets you review and apply fixes without leaving it. It uses the same sign-in as the CLI.
guide.extensionInstall: Install it from the VS Code Marketplace and click the shield in the status bar to scan.
guide.ciNote: CI note: unslop scan exits with a non-zero code when a CRITICAL finding is confirmed — the build fails.

meta.title: Unslop — Deterministic AI Code Review
meta.description: Unslop is the deterministic review gate for AI-generated code. 119 research-backed rules, verdicts no LLM votes on — on every pull request, in your terminal, in your editor.
meta.ogTagline: 119 research-backed rules. Verdicts no LLM votes on.

hero.headline: Your AI reviewer misses 44× more bugs than a <accent>parser</accent>.
hero.bluf: Unslop is the deterministic review gate for AI-generated code. It catches what LLM reviewers miss — on every pull request, in your terminal, and in your editor.
hero.sub: Same files, two reviewers: a cloud LLM found 44× fewer issues than a deterministic scan. We built the gate on the side that wins.
hero.tagline: The only AI code gate that doesn’t ask an AI whether the AI was wrong.

statBand.heading: The research, in numbers
statBand.intro: Backed by independent, published academic research. All sources in the footer.

judgeMiss.caption: fewer issues found by an LLM judge than by a deterministic scan of the same files

severityGap.caption: more high-severity flaws per file in AI-generated code

erosion.caption: vulnerabilities per sample as “improve this code” rounds pile up

selfCorrection.caption: of LLM “self-corrections” actually made code safer

ruleCount.caption: research-backed rules power the Unslop engine

pillarJudge.header: An LLM cannot be your CI gate.
pillarJudge.paragraphOracle: The research is blunt. On identical tasks, deterministic checks reach precision 1.00; LLM judges manage 0.50–0.67 — a coin flip. Change the sampling temperature, and the verdict changes with it. That’s not a gate. That’s a slot machine.
pillarJudge.paragraphSilent: Worse: the misses are silent. LLM judges under-count the most dangerous bugs — failures dressed up as success — by 44 to 1.
pillarJudge.punchline: Unslop decides pass or fail deterministically. The AI explains findings. It never votes on them.

pillarErosion.paragraphRefinement: Measured across refinement rounds, vulnerability density climbs 2.1 → 4.7 → 6.2 per sample. Every round. Even with security-focused prompts.
pillarErosion.paragraphSlopsquatting: And AI doesn’t just write bugs — it invents dependencies. 205,474 hallucinated package names, 43% recurring. A ready-made supply-chain attack surface.
pillarErosion.punchline: Unslop re-checks every revision, not just the final diff. If quality drops, the build fails.

pillarArchitecture.header: Deterministic where it matters. AI where it helps.
pillarArchitecture.paragraphDeterministic: Our proprietary engine runs mechanical checks by machine — perfect precision on tasks where LLM judges top out at 0.67. Behind it: 119 rules, distilled from published research on how AI code actually fails.
pillarArchitecture.paragraphGatedRag: It adapts to your codebase and applies context only where it measurably helps — lifting fix success from 34.4% to 87.1%. We publish the results, not the recipe.

fixGuidance.gate: Names the violated rule — fix rate 34.4% → 87.1%

testsPass.rebuttal: Up to 77% of AI-written test methods assert nothing. High coverage, poor detection. Green CI is not a verdict.

securePrompting.rebuttal: Security prompting changed nothing in Java — and C showed +41–42% more flaws. A prompt is not a control.

demoWorked.rebuttal: 100% of generated OAuth samples hard-coded the client secret. AI code is a happy-path generator.

agentGuardrails.rebuttal: Up to 98.6% of real-world agent denylists were bypassable. Agents need harder gates, not softer ones.

sourceCode.question: Do you store or train on our source code?
sourceCode.answer: We don't train on it, and neither does Google: inference runs on Google Vertex AI under terms that exclude training on customer prompts, on the EU endpoint with processing guaranteed inside EU member states. We do store data: repository indexing keeps only the API surface — exported signatures, interfaces, type definitions — never implementation bodies; reviews operate on the diff of the change under review, and the findings (with the quoted lines) plus, for CLI and MCP scans, the submitted diff are kept as your scan history. GitHub tokens are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. Full details in the privacy policy.

ciSpeed.question: Will this slow down our CI/CD or block our merges?
ciSpeed.answer: No. The webhook is acknowledged instantly and the review runs asynchronously as a native GitHub check run — parallel to your CI, never inside your build. The worst case (full three-model escalation) is hard-capped at 300 seconds; most reviews finish in a single pass. Only CRITICAL findings fail the check; advisory findings conclude as neutral and cannot block a merge. Whether the check is required at all remains your branch-protection decision.

adoption.question: Does my team need to learn another dashboard?
adoption.answer: No. Findings land where your team already works: as check runs and review comments on the pull request, in the terminal via the unslop CLI — it diffs your tracked changes against the merge-base, zero configuration — and in VS Code, where fixes are reviewed and applied without leaving the editor. The dashboard handles configuration and billing, not your daily loop.

determinism.question: Is this just another noisy AI reviewer?
determinism.answer: No. Verdicts come from 119 deterministic rules — the LLM explains findings, it never decides them. Every model call runs at temperature 0, so the same diff always produces the same verdict, and every draft finding must survive a blind verification pass before it reaches your PR.

outage.question: What happens when Unslop itself is down?
outage.answer: Your PRs don’t hang. Every failure path closes the check run explicitly: a crashed review concludes as a failure with the reason in the check output, and a skipped review (quota, deactivated repository) posts a completed check that says why — never an eternal “Expected — waiting for status”. If you mark the check as required, standard GitHub branch-protection overrides still apply.
